title: At one structural position, maxDepth truncates the map and spares the list
rationale: A Map value recurses at depth+1 but a List value recurses at depth. The same configured number means "N map levels" for maps and "N+1 levels" for lists. A user who sets maxDepth to bound memory gets a bound that varies with the shape of their data. Sibling containers at the identical position make the divergence impossible to argue away.
catchesBugClass: Two classes in one document: a bound whose meaning depends on container type, and length-mismatched fields being back-filled with a duplicated last value instead of null.
cannotCatch: It cannot separate the two failures, so the assertion must be on the exact reconstructed structure rather than a boolean. It also cannot tell you WHICH treatment is correct.

predicted.detail: Sibling keys at the same nesting position get opposite treatment, and reconstruction then compounds it by inferring an array and duplicating the stringified map into an element it never occupied.
